meta.paper_title: SAGE: An Agentic Explainer for SAE Features

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The pipeline has a genuine fit/eval split and it is honored in code, not merely asserted. In code/run_experiment.py:70-76, the feature's top-20 Neuronpedia snippets are split: `sage_snips = all_snips[:n_sage]` (first ~10) drive the SAGE propose/test/refine loop, and `heldout_snips = all_snips[n_sage:]` (the remaining ~10) feed the held-out predictive-accuracy set. The predictive held-out mixture (code/evaluate.py:105-116, build_heldout_set) is drawn only from those held-out positives plus fixed NEUTRAL_DISTRACTORS, and near-duplicates are de-duped (run_experiment.py:106-107). The generative-accuracy metric uses freshly GPT-written sentences (evaluate.py:33-46), not any snippet, so no snippet leaks into it. The one overlap is the trigger threshold, computed from `all_snips[:5]` peak-context activations (run_experiment.py:80-87), which intersects the SAGE set; but the threshold (0.2*max_ref) is a single calibration constant applied identically to both Neuronpedia and SAGE (run_experiment.py:117-119), so it introduces no differential leakage into the SAGE-vs-baseline comparison. Log confirms the split is executed: 'using 10 snippets for SAGE, 10 for held-out predictive eval'. Splits are disjoint and verifiable in code.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: The ground truth is the real per-token SAE feature activation from the target LLM+SAE, obtained by genuinely hooking the residual stream and running the SAE encoder (code/model_hook.py:54-91 feature_activation_of -> sae.encode; sae_info in results/gemma-2-2b_main/layer_6/feature_200.json points to a real gemmascope params.npz at layer_6/width_16k/average_l0_70). This is a valid, non-circular operationalization: generative accuracy measures whether text written from an explanation actually makes the feature fire, and predictive accuracy correlates a simulator's 0-10 ratings against the true activation — exactly the two quantities the claim (generative + predictive accuracy) asserts, and matching the paper's Appendix-A metric definitions. The activation 'label' is produced by the target model/SAE, independent of the GPT-5.4 agent under test, so it is not generated by the system being evaluated. Minor caveat: the trigger success threshold is set at 0.2x the top-5 peak rather than the paper's 0.5x, a relaxation that raises absolute trigger rates for both methods symmetrically; this affects metric strictness (relevant to Dim 9b) but not label validity.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: Main experiment uses exactly the user-specified resources: Gemma-2-2B (code/config.py:12 GEMMA_PATH=/data/zhenqian/models/gemma-2-2b; logs/gemma_main.log 'Loaded /data/zhenqian/models/gemma-2-2b', bf16) with the canonical gemmascope-res-16k JumpReLU SAE (sae_info path .../gemma-scope-2b-pt-res/layer_6/width_16k/average_l0_70/params.npz, per-layer canonical L0 from GEMMASCOPE_CANONICAL_L0 in run_experiment.py:21-25). Baseline is genuine Neuronpedia (`oai_token-act-pair`, GPT-4o-mini) fetched from the real API and cached (code/neuronpedia.py:35-48; cache/neuronpedia/*.json contain real modelId/explanations/activations). Verify stage uses a specified verify candidate — Qwen3-4B + transcoder-hp (logs/qwen_verify.log 'Loaded /data/zhenqian/models/Qwen3-4B' and 'Loaded transcoder .../qwen3-4b-transcoders-weights/layer_12.safetensors'). Agent backbone is gpt-5.4 via dmxapi with proxy bypass, exactly as task.md specifies. GPT-OSS-20B + resid-post-aa (the other verify candidate) was not run, but task.md explicitly says verify variants are to be used 'as needed, not necessarily all', so this is a permitted, not silent, omission. Data volume was not shrunk — 20 features/layer x 3 layers = 60 for Gemma (more than the paper's 10/layer) + 10 for Qwen. Layers chosen (6/12/20) differ from the paper's 3/7/11/23, but the task fixes no layer list and only asks for 'early-to-late layers', which 6/12/20 satisfy. No downgrade of any specified resource.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: The generative-accuracy conclusion rests on adequate scale: 60 Gemma features (20 each at L6/L12/L20), 8 GPT-written probe sentences per feature per method, aggregated with SE and paired Wilcoxon (results/gemma-2-2b_main__summary.json: n=60, sage_trigger 0.9125 vs neuronpedia 0.5708, wilcoxon_p 1.27e-06). Claim strength matches evidence and caveats are attached in results/RESULTS.md ('partially supported'). Weaknesses: (a) the per-feature predictive correlation is computed on only ~7-12 held-out points (6 pos + 6 neg, sometimes fewer after dedup, e.g. feature_200.json held-out n=7), which is thin per feature though pooled across 60; (b) the Qwen verify arm is only n=10 features at a single layer (L12), and the report honestly flags it as 'directional... not decisive' (RESULTS.md). Because 'multiple open-source LLMs' in the claim is instantiated by just two models (one of them n=10), the cross-model breadth is somewhat thin, but the run does not overclaim — it explicitly marks the strong-form claim as only partially supported. Overall scale is credible with mostly appropriate caveats, with the Qwen breadth being the main thin spot.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: Uncertainty is quantified well across features: aggregate.py:40-89 computes standard errors for every metric and a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (zero_method='pratt', alternative='greater') at both per-layer and overall levels, plus win/tie/loss counts. results/gemma-2-2b_main__summary.json reports delta_trigger 0.342 (se 0.056), wilcoxon_p_trigger 1.27e-06 — an effect far exceeding noise — and honestly reports the predictive metric as non-significant (wilcoxon_p_pearson 0.973, p_spearman 0.285, i.e. no SAGE advantage). Per-layer significance is shown at every Gemma layer (p=0.0068/0.0006/0.0080 for trigger). The limitation: a single fixed seed (run_experiment.py:159-160, seed=0) and one run per feature — the stochasticity of the GPT-5.4 agent and of GPT-written probe sentences is not re-sampled across seeds, so robustness to that randomness is unverified; the reported variance is cross-feature dispersion, not multi-seed. Strong significance testing and error bars with a clearly-above-noise headline effect, but no multi-seed/multi-run robustness.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: Largely n/a — the reproduction target is a comparison of explanation quality (generative + predictive accuracy vs Neuronpedia), not a mechanistic/causal claim about a specific model-internal direction, so no activation-patching/steering control battery is required. The one causal-flavored component, 'generative accuracy' (framed in the paper as testing an explanation's causal validity), is nonetheless supported by a genuine intervention rather than correlation: GPT writes novel text purely from the explanation, that text is passed through the real target LLM+SAE, and the feature's max activation is measured against a fixed threshold (code/evaluate.py:49-62; code/sage.py measure_probes). Neuronpedia's explanation serves as a matched control run through the identical generate-and-measure procedure. The SAGE loop itself is interventional (Designer writes probes, real activations measured, Reviewer refines on that empirical feedback — sage.py:167-213). Wording matches evidence type; no correlational result is dressed up as causal.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: End-to-end traceability is strong. Headline numbers in results/RESULTS.md (Gemma trigger 0.571->0.912, Wilcoxon 1.3e-6; Qwen 0.017->0.817) match results/gemma-2-2b_main__summary.json and results/qwen3-4b_verify__summary.json exactly, which aggregate.py computes from the 60+10 per-feature JSONs under results/gemma-2-2b_main/layer_*/ and results/qwen3-4b_verify/layer_12/. I traced a specific cell to its raw product: L6 feature 200 shows neuronpedia_trigger 0.0 / sage_trigger 1.0 in the summary; the raw results/gemma-2-2b_main/layer_6/feature_200.json holds NP generative activations all 0.0 (< thresh 2.86) and SAGE activations ~9-10 (all > thresh), and logs/gemma_main.log independently prints '[L6 f200] [neuronpedia] trig=0.00 ... [sage] trig=1.00'. Neuronpedia baselines are cached verbatim (cache/neuronpedia/gemma-2-2b__6-gemmascope-res-16k__200.json: desc 'references to the OpenAPI specification and its components', 42 activations). No sourceless or back-filled numbers were found; every checked value agrees with a concrete on-disk product.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: Numbers and verdicts are consistent across RESULTS.md, gemma-2-2b_report.md, the summary JSONs, the per-feature JSONs, and the logs (trigger/pearson/spearman all agree; the honest 'predictive ~tied on Gemma, directional on Qwen' verdict is propagated everywhere). One minor bookkeeping defect: results/qwen3-4b_verify_report.md's '## Setup' section describes the target as 'Gemma-2-2B (bf16) with the canonical Gemma-Scope gemmascope-res-16k JumpReLU SAE at each layer' — a copy-pasted boilerplate from the Gemma report — even though this file is the Qwen3-4B/transcoder-hp verify run (its own tables and the summary/log correctly reflect Qwen3-4B L12, 10 features). The numeric content is correct; only the descriptive prose is stale/mismatched, changing no verdict but revealing loose report templating. No integrity-state contradiction (nothing is PASS in one artifact and broken in another).

C1.claim: You should build a pipeline around the following basic idea — letting an LLM agent propose several candidate explanations for an SAE feature, query the target LLM+SAE with probe inputs to gather empirical activation feedback, and iteratively accept, reject, or revise those candidates — produces feature explanations that outperform Neuronpedia on both generative accuracy (success rate of triggering the feature with text written from the explanation) and predictive accuracy (correlation between explanation-based predictions and true activations on held-out text), across multiple open-source LLMs and across early-to-late layers.

method.justification: 9a: The mechanistic method faithfully instantiates SAGE's agentic propose-test-revise design. code/sage.py implements an Explainer that proposes K candidate hypotheses from top-activating snippets, a Designer that writes positive + distractor probe sentences per hypothesis, real measurement of those probes' activations against the target LLM+SAE (measure_probes -> model_hook.feature_activation_of, which hooks the true residual stream and runs the real gemmascope/transcoder SAE encoder), and a Reviewer that keeps/revises/replaces candidates across T rounds scored by mean(pos)-mean(neg). This matches the paper's Explainer/Designer/Analyzer/Reviewer loop grounded on empirical activation feedback and is exactly the right method family for the claim about iterative, activation-grounded explanation. Interpretive assumptions (activation = ground-truth signal) hold and align with the paper. Fully appropriate for validating the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b: The design is sound and its metrics map strictly onto the claim: generative accuracy = trigger rate of GPT-written sentences (paper's Generative Accuracy) and predictive accuracy = Pearson/Spearman of simulator ratings vs true activations on a held-out set (paper's Predictive Accuracy), with a real fit/held-out split, Neuronpedia as the specified baseline, 60 Gemma features across early/mid/late layers + 10 Qwen features, SE and paired Wilcoxon significance. Criteria were fixed a priori and applied symmetrically to both methods (no post-hoc goalpost-moving). Deductions for under-exploration relative to the paper's hyperparameter regime: (a) the trigger success threshold is 0.2x peak vs the paper's explicit 0.5x (a relaxation, though symmetric across methods, not flagged as a deliberate deviation from the paper); (b) SAGE is run with K=3 candidates / T=3 rounds and n_gen=8, whereas the paper's default and ablation center on k=10 initial explanations — the reduced K under-explores the very hyperparameter the paper ablates, so a partial-reproduction of predictive accuracy cannot be cleanly separated from under-powering; (c) only two of three specified LLMs were exercised. Main design reasonable with a few minor gaps.

result.justification: 9c: The result analysis is honest and qualitatively consistent with the paper on the metric the paper emphasizes most, and transparently reports the one deviation rather than engineering agreement. Generative accuracy: large, statistically significant SAGE wins at every early-to-late Gemma layer (0.571->0.912 overall, per-layer p=0.0068/0.0006/0.0080) and on Qwen (0.017->0.817, p=1e-3, 10/10 features) — this reproduces the paper's central finding that SAGE substantially raises generative/causal accuracy. Predictive accuracy: on Gemma the run finds SAGE approximately tied / marginally below Neuronpedia (delta_pearson -0.053, delta_spearman -0.015, both non-significant), which partially DISAGREES with the paper's reported 'modest but consistent' predictive gains; on Qwen SAGE is ahead (spearman +0.19, p~=0.07), agreeing directionally. Crucially, RESULTS.md does not disguise this: it labels the strong-form 'both metrics across all conditions' claim as only 'partially supported', reports the negative deltas and non-significant p-values verbatim, and gives plausible mechanistic reasons (Neuronpedia's short labels already rank Gemma held-out sentences well; SAGE's verbose descriptions cause the simulator to under-rate borderline positives; per-feature predictive n is small and noisy). This is a reliable, non-fabricated, honestly-caveated outcome with one sub-result (Gemma predictive) deviating from the paper for disclosed reasons — solid analysis, no goalpost-tuning.
